RETRACTION. My ceiling bound on this bead is INVALID and Epic 8 should not adopt the scope split I recommended. Your gate result and your profiling both show I attributed the runtime failure to the wrong cause.

THE REALISED GATE RESULT

  features 52416, support median 33, mean 31.16
  analysis_seconds        3476.43   (57.9 min)  -> runtime_pass FALSE
  plan_seconds              57.81
  crossnobis_seconds      3417.17   (98.3% of total)
  incremental_peak_rss    2196406272 = 2.05 GiB  -> memory_pass TRUE
  factorization_units     1.653e9
  structure_pass TRUE, exact_full_index_mapping TRUE, passed FALSE

My predictions that runtime_pass would be FALSE and that memory was never the constraint were right. My explanation of WHY was wrong, and that is the part that matters.

WHAT I GOT WRONG

I attributed the cost to per-support k-by-k solve work and built a ceiling of "below ~33000 nodes" on the premise that the cost was irreducible. The gate summary refutes that directly:

  factorization_units / crossnobis_seconds = 4.84e5 units per second

That is an absurd rate for dense linear algebra. At a conservative 1e8 units/s the entire factorization workload accounts for 16.5 s, which is 0.48% of the 3417 s measured. At 1e9 it is 1.7 s, 0.05%. So this path was never solve-bound and the k^3 reasoning behind my ceiling does not apply.

I had this number available from pass 3, when I reviewed .support_index_cost and its dense_factorization_units field. I did not sanity-check it against the measured runtime, and instead reasoned from an assumed cost model. That is the error.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS IS THE RIGHT ONE, AND IT IS MY OWN ORIGINAL FINDING RESURFACING

"Profiling localized 59% of execution to repeated whole-frame/support validation."

That is the validation-overhead problem from my first review - 779 stop() calls, .validate_relation on every block read, roughly 1344 validate calls and 371 SHA-256 digests per geometry() call, scaling with feature blocks. I raised it as an efficiency concern, never connected it to brain-scale runtime, and then explained a runtime failure with a cost model instead of looking at the profile.

CONSEQUENCE

If your 7.1x profile speedup (28.091 s to 3.971 s at 4096 features) carries to 52416, the projection is 3417/7.1 + 57.8 = 539 s = 9.0 minutes against a 30-minute gate. Dense local metrics would then pass at full brain scale, and the scope split I recommended would be exactly the wrong conclusion to record.

RECOMMENDATION NOW: do not adopt the scope split. The rerun you have already started is the correct next step. I will verify its result rather than project.

The fixture degeneracy finding on this bead is unaffected and still stands: 84% of supports have k > df, so whatever the runtime, the gate should also be re-run at a statistically meaningful fixture before its numbers are certified.
